subject: Private deploy: residency & emergency evacuation (EU <-> APAC) - delegated routing proposal
messages:
From: Suzanne Lam <suzanne.lam@bankwest.co.uk>
To: kimberly.park@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 30 May 2028 07:12:00 +0000
Subject: Private deploy: residency & emergency evacuation for EU/APAC workloads

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for taking this on. We're finalizing architecture for a private Redwood deployment that will serve EU retail data and APAC analytics workloads. Two constraints from our compliance team:

- Persistent customer data must never be replicated across an international boundary except under a documented and auditable evacuation event.
- Any failover must preserve proof of custody (KMS separation) and produce an audit trail sufficient for internal auditors and external regulators.

We need a recommended pattern that meets both: low RTO for EU services, warm-standby in APAC for compute, and a clearly auditable cross-border evacuation path that does not automatically sync PII.

Can Redwood provide a network & routing approach (e.g., delegated routing, staged evacuation, egress gating) and an operational playbook we can hand to our infra team? Also include the minimum evidence set we should expect to share with auditors.

Attaching a short residency matrix (residency_matrix.xlsx) that lists data categories. Happy to hop on a 30-min call this week.

Thanks,
Suzanne
Head of Cloud Architecture
BankWest Financial Services

[Attachment: residency_matrix.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)]

From: kimberly.park@redwood.ai
To: Suzanne Lam <suzanne.lam@bankwest.co.uk>
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 30 May 2028 09:18:00 +0200
Subject: Re: Private deploy: residency & emergency evacuation for EU/APAC workloads

Suzanne — appreciate the matrix and context. High level proposal below; I'll follow up with a short MAP and an ops runbook draft.

Executive summary (short):
- Use delegated routing + custody zoning: customer's persistent state (S3-like storage, DB) remains in-region. Control-plane and scheduling can be multi-region, but control-plane must respect custody tokens so cross-border copies do not happen automatically.
- Evacuation model: staged evacuation (Tier 1 -> Tier 2) where Tier 1 (EU primary) can evacuate compute to APAC only after an explicit, auditable "evacuation token" exchange that triggers a read-only snapshot export and a controlled import. No automatic replication.
- Network: egress gating (allowlist) + BGP community tagging to ensure any emergency routes require a signed ticket and route policy change.

Technical bullets for your infra team:
- Data custody: KMS keys per-region with key policy that requires org approval for key export; all backup export actions must be signed and logged.
- Routing: delegated routing layer in the control plane that manages ephemeral east-west circuits; changes require a two-person approval and produce a signed route-change artifact.
- Caching & KV: use in-region KV + prefix cache replication only for non-PII; PII keys are only referenced via region-local KV and cannot be served from remote caches.
- Sync: snapshot-export job with integrity hash and time-stamped audit record; import into APAC is allowed only after verification and expire-after-read staging.
- Canary & test: quarterly evacuation drills; first drill to be a dry-run (routing change + synthetic traffic) then a full-state export/import under a lab account.

Attachments I'm including: residency_matrix.xlsx you sent (kept), plus a small network playbook snippet (network_playbook_snippet.txt) and the initial MAP PDF. I'll also share a draft evacuation_runbook.md for your ops team.

Next steps:
1) Confirm which data categories are strictly in-scope for "no cross-border replication" (from your matrix).
2) Agree on a 2-week window for a tabletop run and a 1-month window for a lab drill.
3) I can join your infra call Thurs 14:00 BST if that works.

Happy to walk through any of the bullets — attached playbook snippet contains a minimal BGP community policy example.

Best,

Kimberly Park
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0172

From: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai

Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai, Suzanne Lam <suzanne.lam@bankwest.co.uk>
Date: Tue, 30 May 2028 11:03:00 +0530
Subject: Re: Private deploy: residency & emergency evacuation for EU/APAC workloads

Couple of concrete operational notes we should bake into the runbook: 

- BGP/community tagging: use a dedicated community (0:6100) that marks routes as "evacuation-pending"; route announcements with that community will be accepted only after a signed ticket from BankWest ops and a control-plane signature from Redwood.
- Egress gating: NACL and managed firewall rule sets should block any egress from region-local storage endpoints except the snapshot export endpoints. Snapshot export endpoints are ephemeral and rotate per-event.
- KMS workflow: leverage per-region CMKs with IAM role that requires MFA + approval binding; export uses a one-time wrap key that is ephemeral and logged to the audit event stream.

I'll paste a short snippet of a maintenance-step here for the playbook: 

--- playbook snippet start ---
1) Raise evacuation ticket in BankWest JIRA: EVAC-<env>-<ts>
2) Redwood issues evacuation-token: signed JSON with expiry and route-change fingerprint
3) BankWest infra applies BGP community 0:6100 to east-west circuit and opens snapshot export endpoint IP range
4) Snapshot job runs -> upload to encrypted staging bucket (region-locally) -> integrity hash + audit event
5) Redwood validates hash and performs controlled one-time import into APAC staging project
6) Post-import verification and manual promote (two-person approve)
--- playbook snippet end ---

We should schedule the first lab drill in a sandbox tenant (no real PII) and then a second mock with anonymized extracts. Happy to own the network steps if Kim approves.

- Rishi
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: network_playbook_snippet.txt (text/plain)]

Thanks — answers inline and next steps below.

1) Evacuation token TTL: default 4 hours (configurable). Tokens are single-use and recorded in the audit stream with the initiating ticket ID. We can reduce TTL to 1 hour for higher assurance.

2) Evidence bundle (we will produce):
- Signed route-change artifact (JSON) with control-plane signature and BGP community change snapshot
- KMS audit events (CMK key-use records and one-time wrap key ID)
- Snapshot integrity hash and upload receipt (hash, size, timestamp)
- Import verification log and promote approval record (two approvers)
- Post-event runbook checklist and incident retrospective note

Attached: MAP_v2.pdf (the mutual action plan that includes schedule options), evacuation_runbook_draft.md (ops steps + playbook).

Proposed timeline:
- Week 0: Agree scope and data-category list (you confirm from your matrix)
- Week 2: Tabletop drill (control-plane routing change only; no exports)
- Week 6: Lab drill with anonymized snapshot export/import

I can join your procurement/infosec sign-off call Thurs 14:00 BST. If that works, I'll present the MAP and go over the evidence bundle.

If you approve, we'll put the MAP in your procurement ticket and schedule the tabletop drill.
